mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last four weeks indicates a strong underlying momentum for recovery, which will continue to drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean of RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days, despite the observed upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week rebound in WORKPLACES mobility, as seen in the latest data, signals a renewed return to office work and associated weekday retail activities, leading to increased RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days following a week where WORKPLACES mobility rose by more than 5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: The combined trend of decreasing time spent at home (RESIDENTIAL) and increasing engagement with outdoor leisure (PARKS) indicates a broader shift towards out-of-home activities, which will positively impact RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL mobility decreasing and PARKS mobility increasing over the same period.

mechanism_narrative: The broad-based recovery across multiple mobility categories including RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES strongly suggests a policy environment of easing restrictions, which will continue to foster increased public activity and drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases, while GROCERY_PHARM, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES mobility also show a decline, indicating a reversal of policy easing.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week increase in TRANSIT station mobility indicates a surge in public transport usage, reflecting increased movement for work and leisure, which will directly translate to higher RETAIL_REC in the immediate next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases in the week following a period where TRANSIT mobility increased by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained upward trend in GROCERY_PHARM mobility over the past four weeks suggests growing public comfort with out-of-home errands and public spaces, which will spill over into increased RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than the previous 14 days, despite GROCERY_PHARM mobility continuing its upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous increase in WORKPLACES mobility and decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility signifies a strong and sustained shift of daily activities from home to external locations, directly boosting foot traffic and spending in retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases, despite WORKPLACES mobility increasing and RESIDENTIAL mobility decreasing over the same period.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility returning to and staying above baseline indicates a strong return to outdoor leisure activities, which often precedes or coincides with increased engagement in other retail and recreation categories, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility has crossed 0% and remains positive for at least two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days declines, even though PARKS mobility has been consistently above baseline for two or more weeks.
